title: Operational Safeguard Collaboration Sprint Horizon
content:
Purpose:
This working plan describes a six-sprint cross-functional program to operationalize a safety-first reliability posture for model-serving surfaces. Goal is to establish clear service-level objectives (SLOs), end-to-end runbooks for graceful degradation, and a transferable handoff path to feature teams and on-call. This doc is intentionally tactical: sprint commitment, minimal deliverables, owners, and acceptance criteria.

Context and motivations:
- Recent outages during high prefix-cache churn exposed gaps in degradation behavior and poor cross-team escalation.
- Platform telemetry shows 2x variance in p50 latency across regions under similar load; customers reported tail-latency impact for embeddings endpoints.
- We must reduce user-visible error rate and stabilize latency SLOs while enabling safe rollback paths for model rollouts.

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
- In-scope: API surface (generation + embeddings), routing fallback policies, latency and availability SLO definitions, monitoring dashboards, runbooks for degradation corridors, CI gating for rollout experiments, quick-fallback hooks.
- Out-of-scope: billing model changes, long-term kernel-level runtime rewrites, large-scale infra purchases.

Primary objectives (outcomes):
1) Define concrete, measured SLOs for three service groups (low-latency chat, batch embedders, streaming generation) with initial baselines and error budget policy.
2) Implement three runbooks: (a) prefix-cache congestion, (b) model-variant fallback, (c) multi-region failover. Each runbook must include decision trees and communication templates.
3) Create observability panels and automated alerts tied to SLO signals and degradation corridors.
4) Deliver an automated canary-to-fallback pipeline (feature teams can declare a canary that will auto-fallback on SLO breach).
5) Handoff package for feature teams with checklist, runbooks, and a 30-day monitoring play.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Program lead: Asha Patel (SRE) — overall coordination, stakeholder alignment.
- Platform eng lead: Michael Chen — routing, autoscaling policies.
- Serving runtime lead: Rajiv Singh — model fallback hooks, KV cache diagnostics.
- Observability lead: Laura Gomez — metrics, dashboards, alerting rules.
- Console/product contact: Emily Zhao — rollout UX and customer communication templates.
- Solutions eng liaison: Tom Becker — customer impact assessment and runbook rehearsal.
- Security/compliance reviewer: Sophie Laurent — review for private deployments and audit requirements.

Working assumptions:
- We can instrument additional SLI counters at the proxy and runtime layers within the first two sprints.
- Feature teams will participate in at least one tabletop and one live rehearsal.
- There is budget for up to two weeks of consultant SRE support if needed for runbook rehearsals.

Six-sprint plan (2-week sprints):
Sprint 0 (planning & baseline) — owner: Asha/Laura
- Kickoff: alignment workshop with feature leads and product.
- Baseline collection: collect 30-day baseline of latency, error-rate, tail percentiles per endpoint.
- Deliverable: Baseline report + candidate SLO targets.

Sprint 1 (SLO definition & measurement) — owner: Laura/Rajiv
- Finalize SLO targets for three service groups; define SLIs and instrumentation gaps.
- Implement missing SLI counters in proxy (requests, errors, latency histograms).
- Deliverable: SLO spec doc and measurement checklist.

Sprint 2 (runbook prototypes & alerting) — owner: Tom/Rajiv
- Draft runbooks for prefix-cache congestion and model-variant fallback.
- Implement alert rules mapped to SLI thresholds and link to runbooks.
- Deliverable: Two runbook drafts, alerts in staging.

Sprint 3 (automated canary and fallback pipeline) — owner: Michael/Emily
- Build and test automated canary gating that triggers immediate fallback when SLOs breach during canary.
- Integrate with console to show canary health and allow manual override.
- Deliverable: Canary pipeline prototype + test plan.

Sprint 4 (observability panels & rehearsals) — owner: Laura/Tom
- Create dedicated dashboards for SLOs, error budgets, and degradation corridors.
- Conduct two tabletop exercises with feature teams; refine runbooks.
- Deliverable: Dashboards, after-action notes.

Sprint 5 (handoff & retention) — owner: Asha/Emily
- Finalize handoff package: runbooks, checklist, oncall play, SLAs, communication templates.
- Prepare retention policy for SLO dashboards and audit artifacts.
- Deliverable: Handoff folder and rollout calendar.

Acceptance criteria (per objective):
- SLOs are codified in a single source-of-truth (Confluence + config repo) and validated against baseline.
- Three runbooks exist with decision trees, expected actions, and timeframe (TTR) estimates.
- Alerts fire in staging and map to a documented escalation ladder with concrete names/contacts.
- Canary pipeline triggers fallback in a repeatable integration test (recorded).
- At least two feature teams sign off on the handoff package and complete a rehearsal within 30 days.

Key metrics and SLIs to track:
- p50/p95/p99 latency per endpoint (generation, streaming, embeddings).
- request success rate (4xx/5xx split) and model-inference-specific error codes.
- prefix-cache miss ratio and KV eviction churn.
- rollback rate during rollouts and mean time to fallback.
- error budget burn rate per service group.

Communication plan and cadence:
- Weekly sync (30 min) with core leads (Asha, Michael, Rajiv, Laura, Emily, Tom) — Monday mornings.
- Bi-weekly cross-team review (45 min) with feature teams and product PMs.
- Incident-style escalation email template and shared Slack channel (#ops-safety-horizon).
- Executive progress brief every sprint review to Growth/Product leadership.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Instrumentation gaps slow measurement. Mitigation: Prioritize implementing lightweight SLIs at proxy layer first and use sampling.
- Risk: Feature teams resist rehearsal time. Mitigation: Offer dedicated solutions-engineer pairing sessions and make rehearsals short and outcome-focused.
- Risk: Auto-fallback may cause regressions (false positives). Mitigation: Implement canary staging with synthetic load tests and require guardrail thresholds before auto-fallback.

Runbook rehearsal checklist (short):
- Confirm chat/bridge setup, primary and secondary contacts.
- Reproduce alert scenario in staging with synthetic traffic.
- Validate decision tree steps complete within TTR estimates.
- Practice public-facing status update and customer messaging.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Final decision on whether to use error-rate or latency as primary SLO for streaming endpoints (deadline: Sprint 1 retro).
- Which alerting signal should trigger auto-fallback vs. manual intervention? Proposal: p99 latency breach sustained for 3 minutes + error budget burn > 20% in 30m window.
- Retention length for SLO telemetry: 90 days vs. 365 days for audits (security to confirm).

Immediate next actions (this week):
1) Schedule kickoff workshop and invite feature leads (owner: Asha).
2) Ask Observability team for 30-day baseline export (owner: Laura).
3) Create SLO spec draft and PR in config repo (owner: Rajiv).
4) Book two tabletop rehearsal slots with Solutions Eng coaching (owner: Tom).

Notes to reviewers: This is a working plan and we expect iteration after the baseline workshop. Please comment inline on the SLO targets section and add any missing stakeholders. If you are a feature team lead, add your preferred rehearsal windows under linked_conference_times in comments.

Appendix (quick references):
- Minimal SLO template: service, SLI, target, measurement window, error budget policy.
- Communication templates: status update, customer impact message, postmortem stub.
summary: Six-sprint tactical program to define SLOs, build runbooks for graceful degradation, implement canary-to-fallback automation, and hand off readiness to feature teams. Owners assigned per sprint and acceptance criteria outlined.
